method: Actual view_image inspection of all six trajectory contact sheets, three native zoom frames, two additional native orbit frames and the two native frames adjacent to the edit switch. Image inspection only; no video playback, new renders or parameter changes.

orbit: All24 thumbnails show a complete lamp with visible shade, stem and base; no thumbnail shows a missing stem or gross cropped/fragmented whole-object shape.
The stem remains a sparse axial support through the inspected orbit. Additional native frames10 and17 retain visibly separated long stem lines despite different apparent line darkness.

Circumferential shade strokes, axial stem strokes and short base cross strokes remain distinct. Base density and shade line darkness vary with view; dark base-front crossings and open patches persist.
No new gross defect that defeats whole-lamp readability is apparent in the sheets or native samples. This observation does not rule out subtle occlusion or raster problems.
zoom: The full object remains comfortably inside every thumbnail across the outward-and-back scale trajectory.
At native frames0,12 and23, including the smallest lamp at frame12, the stem remains nonempty and recognizable as a long axial style; shade and base styles remain readable.
The larger native zoom endpoints disclose fine stair-step/segmented raster appearance on some lines and the inherited uneven base crossings. These do not destroy the complete-object shape.
edit: The sheet shows the dense short-stroke stem for frames0–11 and the sparse long-stroke stem for frames12–23.
Native frames11 and12 make the reduction in clustered dark stem bars clearly visible. The axial hatch remains present after the switch.
Shade outline/strokes and base crosshatching look unchanged across the switch, and the apparent lamp shape stays fixed. Exact pixel locality belongs to independent numerical validation.
The edit is a discrete two-state demonstration; repeated frames around the switch are expected and do not demonstrate continuous transition quality.

scope_limits: This is a bounded trajectory-frame readability review, not a temporal quality or flicker test.
Contact sheets cannot establish no jitter, no popping, temporal correspondence or complete per-stroke visibility correctness.
Video decoding/identity, numeric leakage/coverage and replay results must be reported separately.
Only contact-sheet thumbnails cover every frame; the native samples are explicitly listed. The video streams themselves were not played during this review.
Inherited17 hidden-profile observations, previous failures, GT geometry/manual-direction restrictions and lack of reconstructed input remain unresolved.
p1_progress: The three intended part styles remain readable on the complete object across the saved orbit and zoom frames, and the local stem edit is visibly effective. This removes the conspicuous dense-stem visual obstacle while leaving independent visibility/temporal evidence and reconstructed-input P1 work open.
